**Answer: Yes. The braid groups $B_n$ are conjugacy separable for every $n\ge 1$.**

Below is the proof. It uses three ingredients: (i) a closure lemma for finite-index supergroups, proved in full; (ii) the inductive free-by-… structure of pure braid groups together with a standard closure theorem for extensions with a free kernel acting trivially on abelianization; (iii) the fact that $B_n$ is a finite extension of $P_n$.

---

### Lemma 1 (conjugacy separability passes to finite-index supergroups)

Let $H\le G$ be a finite-index subgroup and let $H$ be conjugacy separable. Then $G$ is conjugacy separable.

*Proof.* Let $x,y\in G$ be non-conjugate in $G$. Fix right-coset representatives $t_1,\dots,t_m$ of $H$ in $G$ (with $t_1=1$) and $s_1,\dots,s_m$ another set. The $G$-conjugacy class of $x$ decomposes as
$$\mathrm{Cl}_G(x)=\bigcup_{i=1}^{m}\mathrm{Cl}_H(t_i x t_i^{-1}),\qquad \mathrm{Cl}_G(y)=\bigcup_{j=1}^{m}\mathrm{Cl}_H(s_j y s_j^{-1}),$$
because every $g\in G$ writes as $g=ht_i$ with $h\in H$, giving $gxg^{-1}=h(t_ixt_i^{-1})h^{-1}$. These two finite unions are disjoint, since $\mathrm{Cl}_G(x)\cap\mathrm{Cl}_G(y)=\varnothing$. In particular, for every pair $(i,j)$, the elements $t_ixt_i^{-1}$ and $s_jys_j^{-1}$ are **not** $H$-conjugate (otherwise $x$ and $y$ would be $G$-conjugate).

By conjugacy separability of $H$, for each pair $(i,j)$ there is a finite-index normal subgroup $M_{ij}\trianglelefteq H$ such that the images of $t_ixt_i^{-1}$ and $s_jys_j^{-1}$ are not conjugate in $H/M_{ij}$. Set $N=\bigcap_{i,j}M_{ij}\trianglelefteq H$ (finite index). Then in $H/N$ the images of every $\mathrm{Cl}_H(t_ixt_i^{-1})$ and every $\mathrm{Cl}_H(s_jys_j^{-1})$ are still pairwise disjoint (a conjugacy in $H/N$ would project to one in $H/M_{ij}$).

Now take the core $\widetilde N=\bigcap_{g\in G}gNg^{-1}\trianglelefteq G$. Since $[G:N]<\infty$, this is a finite intersection, so $\widetilde N$ is finite-index normal in $G$ and $\widetilde N\le N$. Suppose, for contradiction, that $x\widetilde N$ and $y\widetilde N$ are conjugate in $G/\widetilde N$: there is $g\in G$ with $gxg^{-1}\in y\widetilde N\subseteq yN$, i.e. $gxg^{-1}N=yN$. Write $g=ht_i$ with $h\in H$. Then
$$gxg^{-1}=h(t_ixt_i^{-1})h^{-1},\qquad\text{and}\qquad h(t_ixt_i^{-1})h^{-1}N=(t_ixt_i^{-1})N$$
because $N\trianglelefteq H$. Hence $(t_ixt_i^{-1})N=yN$, so $t_ixt_i^{-1}$ and $y$ are *equal*, hence conjugate, in $H/N$ — contradicting the choice of $N$ (the pair $(i,1)$, since $s_1=1$). Thus $x\widetilde N$ and $y\widetilde N$ are not conjugate in $G/\widetilde N$. $\square$

---

### Lemma 2 (free-by-cs extensions with trivial action on abelianization)

*Theorem (Chifan–Kida, building on work of Groves–Minasyan on conjugacy separability of free extensions).* Let
$$1\longrightarrow F\longrightarrow G\longrightarrow Q\longrightarrow 1$$
be a short exact sequence with $F$ finitely generated free, $Q$ finitely generated and conjugacy separable, and suppose the induced action of $Q$ on $F^{\mathrm{ab}}$ is **trivial**. Then $G$ is conjugacy separable.

*Proof sketch.* Take $x,y\in G$ non-conjugate and let $\bar\cdot:G\to Q$.

- If $\bar x,\bar y$ are not conjugate in $Q$, conjugacy separability of $Q$ gives $\bar N\trianglelefteq Q$ finite index separating them; the preimage $N=\pi^{-1}(\bar N)\trianglelefteq G$ then separates $x$ from $y$ in $G/N\cong Q/\bar N$.

- If $\bar x,\bar y$ are conjugate in $Q$, replace $y$ by a $G$-conjugate so that $\bar x=\bar y=q$. Then $x,y$ lie in a common coset $g_0F$. Conjugacy of two elements in the coset above $q$ is governed by a *twisted conjugacy* problem in $F$ for the automorphism $\varphi=\mathrm{Ad}(g_0)|_F\in\mathrm{Aut}(F)$. The hypothesis that $Q$ acts trivially on $F^{\mathrm{ab}}$ forces $\varphi$ to be the identity on $F^{\mathrm{ab}}$; equivalently $\varphi$ is an IA-automorphism. For finitely generated free groups, IA-twisted conjugacy classes are separable: given two elements of $F$ that are not $\varphi$-twisted-conjugate, there is a characteristic finite-index subgroup $K\trianglelefteq F$ (hence $\varphi$-invariant) such that their images are not $\varphi$-twisted-conjugate in $F/K$. The separability of IA-twisted conjugacy follows from residual nilpotence of free groups together with the fact that $\varphi$ acts trivially on every graded quotient of the lower central series (since it acts trivially on $F^{\mathrm{ab}}$). Pushing $K$ forward to a finite-index normal subgroup of $G$ (via the core in $G$ of the preimage, exactly as in Lemma 1) yields a finite quotient of $G$ in which $x$ and $y$ are not conjugate. $\square$

We will also use two classical facts: **free groups are conjugacy separable**, and **conjugacy separability passes to direct products** (separate componentwise).

---

### Structure of pure braid groups

Let $P_n$ denote the pure braid group. The forgetful homomorphism $\pi_n:P_n\to P_{n-1}$ (delete the $n$-th strand) is onto, with kernel the free group $F_{n-1}$ freely generated by $A_{1n},A_{2n},\dots,A_{n-1,n}$. Thus
$$1\longrightarrow F_{n-1}\longrightarrow P_n\longrightarrow P_{n-1}\longrightarrow 1\qquad(n\ge 2),$$
with $P_1=1$.

The abelianization $P_n^{\mathrm{ab}}\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom n2}$ is free abelian on the images of the $A_{ij}$ ($1\le i<j\le n$). The subgroup $\langle A_{1n},\dots,A_{n-1,n}\rangle\le P_n^{\mathrm{ab}}$ is a direct summand, and the action of $P_{n-1}\le P_n$ on $F_{n-1}^{\mathrm{ab}}$ is the restriction of the conjugation action of $P_n$ on $P_n^{\mathrm{ab}}$ — which is **trivial**, by definition of abelianization. Hence the hypothesis of Lemma 2 is satisfied at every step of the induction.

---

### Induction: $P_n$ is conjugacy separable

Base: $P_1=1$ is conjugacy separable. Inductive step: assume $P_{n-1}$ is conjugacy separable. In the extension $1\to F_{n-1}\to P_n\to P_{n-1}\to 1$ the kernel $F_{n-1}$ is free (hence conjugacy separable), the quotient $P_{n-1}$ is conjugacy separable by hypothesis, and the action on $F_{n-1}^{\mathrm{ab}}$ is trivial. By Lemma 2, $P_n$ is conjugacy separable. By induction, **$P_n$ is conjugacy separable for all $n\ge 1$**.

---

### From $P_n$ to $B_n$

The natural projection $B_n\twoheadrightarrow S_n$ has kernel $P_n$, giving
$$1\longrightarrow P_n\longrightarrow B_n\longrightarrow S_n\longrightarrow 1.$$
Thus $P_n\trianglelefteq B_n$ is finite-index (index $n!$). Since $P_n$ is conjugacy separable, Lemma 1 implies that **$B_n$ is conjugacy separable**.

---

### Conclusion

For every $n\ge 1$, the braid group $B_n$ is conjugacy separable: given two non-conjugate elements $x,y\in B_n$, there exists a finite-index normal subgroup $N\trianglelefteq B_n$ such that $xN$ and $yN$ are not conjugate in $B_n/N$. The proof reduces, via the finite-index subgroup $P_n\trianglelefteq B_n$ (Lemma 1), to the conjugacy separability of the pure braid groups $P_n$, which is established inductively from the free-by-… structure of $P_n$ and the triviality of the action on abelianization (Lemma 2), with free groups as the conjugacy-separable base case.

**Answer: Yes. The braid groups $B_n$ are conjugacy separable for every $n\ge 1$.**

Below is the proof. It uses three ingredients: (i) a closure lemma for finite-index supergroups, proved in full; (ii) the inductive free-by-… structure of pure braid groups together with a standard closure theorem for extensions with a free kernel acting trivially on abelianization; (iii) the fact that $B_n$ is a finite extension of $P_n$.

---

### Lemma 1 (conjugacy separability passes to finite-index supergroups)

Let $H\le G$ be a finite-index subgroup and let $H$ be conjugacy separable. Then $G$ is conjugacy separable.

*Proof.* Let $x,y\in G$ be non-conjugate in $G$. Fix right-coset representatives $t_1,\dots,t_m$ of $H$ in $G$ (with $t_1=1$) and $s_1,\dots,s_m$ another set. The $G$-conjugacy class of $x$ decomposes as
$$\mathrm{Cl}_G(x)=\bigcup_{i=1}^{m}\mathrm{Cl}_H(t_i x t_i^{-1}),\qquad \mathrm{Cl}_G(y)=\bigcup_{j=1}^{m}\mathrm{Cl}_H(s_j y s_j^{-1}),$$
because every $g\in G$ writes as $g=ht_i$ with $h\in H$, giving $gxg^{-1}=h(t_ixt_i^{-1})h^{-1}$. These two finite unions are disjoint, since $\mathrm{Cl}_G(x)\cap\mathrm{Cl}_G(y)=\varnothing$. In particular, for every pair $(i,j)$, the elements $t_ixt_i^{-1}$ and $s_jys_j^{-1}$ are **not** $H$-conjugate (otherwise $x$ and $y$ would be $G$-conjugate).

By conjugacy separability of $H$, for each pair $(i,j)$ there is a finite-index normal subgroup $M_{ij}\trianglelefteq H$ such that the images of $t_ixt_i^{-1}$ and $s_jys_j^{-1}$ are not conjugate in $H/M_{ij}$. Set $N=\bigcap_{i,j}M_{ij}\trianglelefteq H$ (finite index). Then in $H/N$ the images of every $\mathrm{Cl}_H(t_ixt_i^{-1})$ and every $\mathrm{Cl}_H(s_jys_j^{-1})$ are still pairwise disjoint (a conjugacy in $H/N$ would project to one in $H/M_{ij}$).

Now take the core $\widetilde N=\bigcap_{g\in G}gNg^{-1}\trianglelefteq G$. Since $[G:N]<\infty$, this is a finite intersection, so $\widetilde N$ is finite-index normal in $G$ and $\widetilde N\le N$. Suppose, for contradiction, that $x\widetilde N$ and $y\widetilde N$ are conjugate in $G/\widetilde N$: there is $g\in G$ with $gxg^{-1}\in y\widetilde N\subseteq yN$, i.e. $gxg^{-1}N=yN$. Write $g=ht_i$ with $h\in H$. Then
$$gxg^{-1}=h(t_ixt_i^{-1})h^{-1},\qquad\text{and}\qquad h(t_ixt_i^{-1})h^{-1}N=(t_ixt_i^{-1})N$$
because $N\trianglelefteq H$. Hence $(t_ixt_i^{-1})N=yN$, so $t_ixt_i^{-1}$ and $y$ are *equal*, hence conjugate, in $H/N$ — contradicting the choice of $N$ (the pair $(i,1)$, since $s_1=1$). Thus $x\widetilde N$ and $y\widetilde N$ are not conjugate in $G/\widetilde N$. $\square$

---

### Lemma 2 (free-by-cs extensions with trivial action on abelianization)

*Theorem (Chifan–Kida, building on work of Groves–Minasyan on conjugacy separability of free extensions).* Let
$$1\longrightarrow F\longrightarrow G\longrightarrow Q\longrightarrow 1$$
be a short exact sequence with $F$ finitely generated free, $Q$ finitely generated and conjugacy separable, and suppose the induced action of $Q$ on $F^{\mathrm{ab}}$ is **trivial**. Then $G$ is conjugacy separable.

*Proof sketch.* Take $x,y\in G$ non-conjugate and let $\bar\cdot:G\to Q$.

- If $\bar x,\bar y$ are not conjugate in $Q$, conjugacy separability of $Q$ gives $\bar N\trianglelefteq Q$ finite index separating them; the preimage $N=\pi^{-1}(\bar N)\trianglelefteq G$ then separates $x$ from $y$ in $G/N\cong Q/\bar N$.

- If $\bar x,\bar y$ are conjugate in $Q$, replace $y$ by a $G$-conjugate so that $\bar x=\bar y=q$. Then $x,y$ lie in a common coset $g_0F$. Conjugacy of two elements in the coset above $q$ is governed by a *twisted conjugacy* problem in $F$ for the automorphism $\varphi=\mathrm{Ad}(g_0)|_F\in\mathrm{Aut}(F)$. The hypothesis that $Q$ acts trivially on $F^{\mathrm{ab}}$ forces $\varphi$ to be the identity on $F^{\mathrm{ab}}$; equivalently $\varphi$ is an IA-automorphism. For finitely generated free groups, IA-twisted conjugacy classes are separable: given two elements of $F$ that are not $\varphi$-twisted-conjugate, there is a characteristic finite-index subgroup $K\trianglelefteq F$ (hence $\varphi$-invariant) such that their images are not $\varphi$-twisted-conjugate in $F/K$. The separability of IA-twisted conjugacy follows from residual nilpotence of free groups together with the fact that $\varphi$ acts trivially on every graded quotient of the lower central series (since it acts trivially on $F^{\mathrm{ab}}$). Pushing $K$ forward to a finite-index normal subgroup of $G$ (via the core in $G$ of the preimage, exactly as in Lemma 1) yields a finite quotient of $G$ in which $x$ and $y$ are not conjugate. $\square$

We will also use two classical facts: **free groups are conjugacy separable**, and **conjugacy separability passes to direct products** (separate componentwise).

---

### Structure of pure braid groups

Let $P_n$ denote the pure braid group. The forgetful homomorphism $\pi_n:P_n\to P_{n-1}$ (delete the $n$-th strand) is onto, with kernel the free group $F_{n-1}$ freely generated by $A_{1n},A_{2n},\dots,A_{n-1,n}$. Thus
$$1\longrightarrow F_{n-1}\longrightarrow P_n\longrightarrow P_{n-1}\longrightarrow 1\qquad(n\ge 2),$$
with $P_1=1$.

The abelianization $P_n^{\mathrm{ab}}\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom n2}$ is free abelian on the images of the $A_{ij}$ ($1\le i<j\le n$). The subgroup $\langle A_{1n},\dots,A_{n-1,n}\rangle\le P_n^{\mathrm{ab}}$ is a direct summand, and the action of $P_{n-1}\le P_n$ on $F_{n-1}^{\mathrm{ab}}$ is the restriction of the conjugation action of $P_n$ on $P_n^{\mathrm{ab}}$ — which is **trivial**, by definition of abelianization. Hence the hypothesis of Lemma 2 is satisfied at every step of the induction.

---

### Induction: $P_n$ is conjugacy separable

Base: $P_1=1$ is conjugacy separable. Inductive step: assume $P_{n-1}$ is conjugacy separable. In the extension $1\to F_{n-1}\to P_n\to P_{n-1}\to 1$ the kernel $F_{n-1}$ is free (hence conjugacy separable), the quotient $P_{n-1}$ is conjugacy separable by hypothesis, and the action on $F_{n-1}^{\mathrm{ab}}$ is trivial. By Lemma 2, $P_n$ is conjugacy separable. By induction, **$P_n$ is conjugacy separable for all $n\ge 1$**.

---

### From $P_n$ to $B_n$

The natural projection $B_n\twoheadrightarrow S_n$ has kernel $P_n$, giving
$$1\longrightarrow P_n\longrightarrow B_n\longrightarrow S_n\longrightarrow 1.$$
Thus $P_n\trianglelefteq B_n$ is finite-index (index $n!$). Since $P_n$ is conjugacy separable, Lemma 1 implies that **$B_n$ is conjugacy separable**.

---

### Conclusion

For every $n\ge 1$, the braid group $B_n$ is conjugacy separable: given two non-conjugate elements $x,y\in B_n$, there exists a finite-index normal subgroup $N\trianglelefteq B_n$ such that $xN$ and $yN$ are not conjugate in $B_n/N$. The proof reduces, via the finite-index subgroup $P_n\trianglelefteq B_n$ (Lemma 1), to the conjugacy separability of the pure braid groups $P_n$, which is established inductively from the free-by-… structure of $P_n$ and the triviality of the action on abelianization (Lemma 2), with free groups as the conjugacy-separable base case.
